name: Granular buffer core from the ground up: grain size/shape/pitch, regular vs random density, triggered grains as a voice, position delay, freeze scrubbing, partial re-freeze, random pan, two feedback modes
goal: Understand and drive a buffer-based granular processor (the kind we need as a Web Audio module) with reverb and feedback turned down first: grains are tens-of-ms-to-1-s micro-samples plucked from a rolling 1–8 s input buffer; set size, shape (gate → triangle → Hann for overlap), pitch; density from noon (none) toward regular spacing one way and random spacing the other, or fire grains from a trigger with sequenced pitch to make a playable voice; use position as a buffer read point (= delay, newest at one end), freeze to scrub inside captured audio, gate the freeze with semi-random gates to partially overwrite and blend the buffer, mind lo-fi buffer modes (low sample rate → low-pass before input; mu-law 8-bit → keep input mid-level), random L/R grain pan for mono→stereo, and know that feedback is true input feedback when live but a separate delay/all-pass diffuser when frozen.

source.title: Clouds (and clones) from the Ground Up: a reverbless explanation of a Granular icon

prerequisites: Granular processor with input buffer, freeze, position, size, shape/texture, pitch, density, trigger input (Web Audio: AudioWorklet ring buffer + windowed grain scheduler, implementation note)
A gate/trigger source and pitch sequencer/quantizer for the voice demo
Speech/radio/varied audio source for position demos

inputs.name: input_audio
inputs.description: Audio to capture into the granular buffer

outputs.name: granular_output
outputs.description: Grain stream: voice, scrub texture or evolving frozen bed (stereo with random pan)

constraints: Original synthesis recipe; not affiliated with any vendor named in the source. Recreate in browser/Web Audio (Polyrhythm Studio) or any hybrid synth with comparable modules; no presets, banks or samples copied.
Start with internal feedback and reverb DOWN — they obscure what the granular core is doing; add external reverb later (internal reverb only affects the granular output).
Lo-fi buffer modes trade fidelity for time: 16 kHz sampling caps content at 8 kHz (low-pass the input to reduce aliasing); 8-bit mu-law favours mid levels — keep input around mid-scale on the meter.
Stereo mode halves record time; L and R are granularized separately only with internal reverb off and random pan at minimum.
Saved buffers are raw material, not presets — reloading won't reproduce a performance.

steps.action: Turn internal feedback and reverb down. Feed a simple source (sine) and listen to individual grains.

Grain structure: size sets grain length (tens of ms → ~1 s); shape/texture morphs from no contour (gate) through triangle to Hann-like windows; use gate-like shapes for individual grains and Hann for overlapping grains; pitch shifts each grain up/down.
steps.expect: Audible change in grain length, envelope smoothness and pitch

steps.action: Grain generation: density at noon = no grains; one direction = evenly spaced grains getting faster until they overlap; the other = randomly spaced grains until they overlap. Fine control near noon matters for counting individual grains.

Triggered voice: density at noon, feed clock-derived gates into the trigger input and quantized pitch per grain from a random/looping sequencer; send an occasional pulse into size to lengthen some notes.
steps.expect: Granular processor behaves like a playable synth voice with some long notes

steps.action: Position: switch to a varied source (speech/radio). Small grains + enough density reconstructs the input; moving position away from the newest end adds a growing delay (there's always a tiny conversion delay at minimum).
steps.expect: Position works as a read point/delay into the rolling buffer

steps.action: Freeze (fully wet): buffer stops updating; the same grain repeats at the current position; shrink size from a whole word to a tiny tone, then sweep position to scrub through captured audio (note: newest audio sits at one end, so 'forward' playback means moving position toward the older end).
steps.expect: Scrubbing inside a captured phrase; tiny grains become tones

steps.action: Evolving buffer: gate the freeze input with semi-random gates so it briefly unfreezes, writing a few seconds of new audio at the front while the rest of the buffer is kept.
steps.expect: Buffer contents blend old and new material over time

steps.action: Post-processing: set wet/dry blend; use random L/R grain panning to turn a mono input into a stereo output; add reverb externally if preferred.
steps.expect: Stereo granular image without internal reverb wash

steps.action: Feedback: when live, it's true feedback of output into the buffer input (can run away — tame by modulating size/position); when frozen, feedback becomes a separate delay + all-pass diffusion that sounds reverb-like without altering the buffer. Watch for jumps when unfreezing.
steps.expect: Controlled feedback in both modes; no explosion on unfreeze

verification: With density at noon and no triggers, output is silent.
Frozen buffer + position sweep scrubs recognizable fragments of the source.
Random pan produces a stereo output from a mono input (L≠R).
Toggling freeze while feedback is up does not cause runaway level.
